# Non-destructive plan retention preview, 2026-10-04

This bounded PROD-OPS-07 slice adds an explicit, typed preview to the existing encrypted-plan store and artifact janitor. It copies no artifact and removes no content or metadata. A possible archive review means only that an operator could later review a copy which preserves the original. No deletion, unlink, pruning implementation, default retention duration, public capability, constructor registration or destructive policy is introduced. User approval remains required for any later destructive policy. The full requirement remains open.

The isolated candidate starts at 09301572a58a1418a8c576d98eb02d440595065c. It owns only the plan-artifacts repository, plan-janitor, execution worker, focused native retention test, additive worker tests and this handoff. Other source, migration history, audit/evidence repositories, custody formats, immutable artifact/association triggers, provider receipts and replay tombstones remain read-only dependencies. Later coherent root corrections are separate source dependencies; this packet must be merged by exact incremental delta rather than overwriting whole newer files.

The existing worker opens its store through openExecutionStore and passes that same handle to maintenance. An absent ZENITH_WORKER_PLAN_RETENTION_PREVIEW variable disables the new preview. An explicitly present value must be a bounded JSON object with exactly workspaceId, createdBefore, limit and holdOperationIds. The cutoff is an explicit canonical UTC timestamp, the batch is an explicit integer 1..1000, and holds are at most 1000 unique bounded native identifiers. There is no inferred cutoff or duration. The captured configuration and hold list are immutable. Invalid configuration refuses before codec, health listener, store opening and polling effects; neither diagnostics nor worker result logs expose input values. Existing legacy directory inspection and its historical age knob are unchanged.

The repository captures own data properties without invoking a configuration or hold accessor. One fresh owning SQL statement selects at most limit+1 original artifact owners from one workspace in stable creation-time/operation order. It selects classification data, never manifest, ciphertext, raw bytes, source/state/storage keys or encryption material. The result contains only mode, scanned count, hasMore and mutually exclusive held, unavailable, active, unresolved, withinRetention and archiveReview counts. At most limit entries contribute counts. A true hasMore is an incomplete-window warning, not a complete inventory or automatic continuation. Repeated previews start from the same oldest window; there is no new pagination or fleet orphan framework. SQL joins may inspect all relevant associations of each bounded owner, so the batch bounds work items rather than claiming a fixed database query cost.

An explicit hold on the source or its same-workspace associated destination protects original custody. A current nonterminal owner or associated destination is active. Missing use rows or unrecognized state refuse archive classification. Claimed, dispatched and uncertain use phases, uncertain operations, unconfirmed permanent workflow attempts and nonterminal build launches remain unresolved. Source creation must precede the explicit cutoff, source artifact expiry must have elapsed, and associated custody must also have expired before archive review. Completed recovery inventory can coexist with a copy review because every acknowledged start, terminal build receipt and original custody row remains intact.

Preview holds are configuration holds for classification, not durable operator hold-management records. They grant no tenant access, cleanup authority or lifetime extension. Existing logical expiry remains unchanged and can make a ready use expired or dispatched use uncertain even when its bytes are held. The artifact janitor still runs expiry first, reports optional count-only preview second, stays single-flight and awaits active work at shutdown. Preview failure yields only the existing unavailable maintenance report. No retention caller can reopen a dispatched or uncertain attempt, alter an approval, drop a receipt or recycle a permanent start/build tombstone.

The native suite uses canonical migrations and two actual PostgreSQL pools. Its encrypted artifact, association and permanent receipt rows are explicitly synthetic storage fixtures, inserted only for native classification and immutable-table checks. They establish no genuine OpenTofu publication, accepted provider call, Temporal retained history, browser consent, hosted topology or credential authority. Cases cover terminal archive review, every active status, uncertain/claimed/dispatched states, missing uses, source and destination holds, active/unresolved/live associations, explicit cutoff and expiry, bounded incomplete windows, tenant isolation, captured holds across a paused native query, independent committed owner changes, unconfirmed start/build inventory, row preservation and immutable tombstone deletion refusal. The preservation case compares whole operation/custody/use/audit/evidence/idempotency/lease/start/build rows before and after preview. A separate existing-expiry invocation verifies that holds preserve bytes without extending execution lifetime.

There are 27 new native case identities and 27 additive configuration/timer model identities. Worker/configuration tests retain the entire existing 14-case legacy janitor suite. New cases explicitly model the timer and repository failures, validate configuration and own-property refusal, and inspect early worker wiring. Their successful preview replies are models, not native evidence. Author project imports, compiler, lint, tests, services, PostgreSQL, Docker, installations and commits are all unrun. Only source and Git/Python integrity checks are performed before freeze.

Root must run pinned Node 22 compilation, scoped ESLint and the two affected suites with maxWorkers=1. Actual PostgreSQL admission uses ZENITH_TEST_PLAN_RETENTION_REQUIRED=1 plus an explicitly owned ZENITH_TEST_PLATFORM_PG_URL; missing native prerequisites fail when required. No PGlite reply supplies those cases. The native case identities and counts in CASE-CONTRACT.json need a separate canonical manifest registration before a required full-lane claim. Existing current coherent root907/80/package22 identities must be preserved during later integration; this packet makes no manifest edits to its older clean093 source baseline.

Independent C/source review and actual root execution remain required. Full archival storage/recovery, durable hold management, physical bounded pruning, operator policy review and destructive approval, hosted build/state retention, full operational rehearsal and release acceptance are outside this slice. All 78 production requirements remain tracked; this source packet completes none by itself.
